title: Area III review: Air Traffic Control Clearances and Procedures
intro: These questions mix both Tasks of Area III: ATC clearances and holding. Many of them join the two in one real IFR flight, from copying a clearance to leaving a hold, just like the checkride.

questions.q: At 7,000 ft, Center says: 'Hold southwest of the BRAVO VOR on the 230 radial, expect further clearance 1450.' Nothing else is said about the hold. How do you fly it?
options: Inbound course 230°, right turns, 1-minute inbound legs
Inbound course 050°, left turns, 1½-minute inbound legs
Inbound course 050°, right turns, 1-minute inbound legs
Inbound course 230°, left turns, 1-minute outbound legs every lap
questions.why: You hold on the 230 radial southwest of the VOR, so you fly inbound toward the station on 050°. An uncharted hold clearance states turns only for left turns, on request, or when the controller thinks it necessary [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8i]] [[33:383|AIM 5-3-8i5]], so fly right turns unless left turns are assigned [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. At or below 14,000 ft MSL the inbound leg is 1 minute [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(a)]].

questions.q: Level at 10,000 ft, you get: 'Descend now to 8,000, cross HAMER at or below 6,000, descend and maintain 4,000.' How should you fly this?
options: Descend promptly to 8,000. Then descend as you like, but be at or below 6,000 at HAMER. After HAMER, descend at normal rates to 4,000.
Descend at your own pace all the way to 4,000, as long as you are at or below 6,000 when you cross HAMER.
Stay at 10,000 until close to HAMER, then descend at pilot's discretion to cross it at or below 6,000.
Descend promptly to 8,000 and hold it until HAMER. After HAMER, descend at normal rates to 4,000.
questions.why: 'Descend now' means start promptly and finish the descent to that altitude. After that, descent to the crossing fix is at pilot's discretion, but you must meet the crossing restriction. After the fix you descend at the suggested rates to the assigned altitude [[33:281|AIM 4-4-10e Example 5]]. Holding 8,000 until HAMER would miss the 'at or below 6,000' restriction.

questions.q: In IMC you are holding at the IAF for your approach, the clearance limit. Your EFC is 1625. You took off at 1340 with a filed time en route of 2 hours 20 minutes. At 1545 your radios fail. When do you start the approach?
options: 1600, your ETA from the filed time en route
At once, because a radio failure in IMC is always an emergency
1655, 30 minutes after the EFC, so ATC can clear the airspace
1625, as close as possible to your EFC
questions.why: Your ETA would be 1340 + 2:20 = 1600, but the ETA is used only when no EFC was received. When the clearance limit is a fix where an approach begins, start descent and the approach as close as possible to the EFC time if you got one [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)(i)]]. Squawk 7600 while you do it [[34:54|AIM 6-4-2]].

questions.q: No hold is charted at your clearance limit, LUMAR, and you have no holding instructions. You are 5 minutes from LUMAR and ATC has said nothing more. What is the best plan?
options: Wait. ATC must give you holding instructions at least 3 minutes before the fix.
Ask ATC for holding instructions now, and start slowing to holding speed when 3 minutes or less from LUMAR.
Turn toward your destination, since a clearance limit ends 5 minutes before you reach it.
Start a standard hold right now on the course you are flying, before you reach LUMAR.
questions.why: With no charted hold and no instructions, ask ATC for holding instructions before you reach the fix. At 3 minutes or less from a clearance limit with no clearance beyond it, start slowing so you cross the fix at or below maximum holding speed [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8c]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]]. Only if you can't get instructions do you hold in a standard pattern on the course you flew to the fix [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8c]].

questions.q: ATC says: 'Hold north of the KELLY VOR on the 360 radial, left turns, expect further clearance 1530.' You will reach the VOR on a heading of 300°. Which entry do you fly?
options: Direct: cross the VOR and turn left to 360° outbound
Teardrop: cross the VOR and fly about 330° for 1 minute
Parallel: fly 360° on the west side for 1 minute, then turn right back toward the holding side
Parallel: fly 360° on the east side for 1 minute, then turn left back toward the holding side
questions.why: Inbound course is 180° and the turns are left, so the holding side is east. A left-turn hold is the mirror image of a standard one: entries are drawn off the 70° line on the holding side [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]]. Here the teardrop sector covers headings 360° to 070°, the parallel sector 250° to 360°, and the rest is direct [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]]. At 300° you fly a parallel entry: parallel the holding course outbound on the nonholding (west) side for 1 minute, then turn toward the holding side through more than 180° to return to the fix or intercept the inbound course [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]].

questions.q: On top of a layer in clear skies, you ask for and get 'maintain VFR-on-top.' Your magnetic course is 115°, and you are more than 3,000 ft above the ground. Which is true?
options: Fly an odd thousand plus 500, like 5,500, and still follow IFR rules such as minimum IFR altitudes and position reports.
Fly any altitude you like, because your IFR flight plan is canceled until you ask for an altitude again.
Fly an even thousand plus 500, like 6,500, and ATC still keeps you apart from other IFR traffic.
Keep your last assigned IFR altitude, but you only need to stay clear of clouds now.
questions.why: VFR-on-top means VFR cruising altitudes and VFR cloud clearances, plus the IFR rules that still apply: minimum IFR altitudes, position reports and your clearance. It does not cancel your IFR flight plan [[33:279|AIM 4-4-8]]. On a magnetic course of 0° to 179° you fly an odd thousand plus 500 [[60:467|14 CFR 91.159(a)(1)]]. Outside Class B or a TRSA, ATC does not separate you from other IFR aircraft while VFR-on-top [[33:282|AIM 4-4-11b]].

questions.q: At 1500 you have 25 gallons and burn 10 GPH in every phase of flight. After the hold you need 15 minutes for the approach and landing, 30 minutes to your alternate, and a 45-minute reserve. What is the latest EFC you can accept and still keep that fuel?
questions.why: 25 gal at 10 GPH = 150 minutes. After the hold you need 15 + 30 + 45 = 90 minutes, so you can hold for 150 - 90 = 60 minutes: 1500 + 60 = 1600. This is the IFR fuel rule: fuel to the destination, then to the alternate, then 45 minutes at normal cruise [[60:468|14 CFR 91.167(a)]] [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]]. 1645 forgets the reserve, 1615 the approach, and 1630 the alternate. Keep a time and fuel record in flight [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].

questions.q: On a STAR, the chart says to 'expect' to cross MIKEY at 11,000. You were only cleared 'via the arrival.' You start down from 13,000 and report 'leaving one three thousand.' Center says 'roger.' Is your descent approved?
options: Yes. ATC heard your report and did not object.
No. 'Roger' only means ATC got your call, and an 'expect' altitude is not a clearance.
Yes. 'Expect' altitudes become crossing restrictions once you are near the fix.
No, but you may keep descending as long as you stay above the MEA.
questions.why: 'Expect' altitudes are for planning and are not crossing restrictions until ATC issues them [[33:393|AIM 5-4-1]]. The IPH tells of a pilot who did this; 'roger' only means ATC received the transmission, not that it understood or approved it. When in doubt, ask ATC [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. You must keep the last assigned altitude until cleared to descend [[33:393|AIM 5-4-1]].

questions.q: ATC tells you to hold at 14,000 ft MSL. No speed icon is shown on the chart. What maximum holding speed and inbound leg time apply?
options: 265 KIAS and 1½ minutes
230 KIAS and 1½ minutes
200 KIAS and 1 minute
230 KIAS and 1 minute
questions.why: From 6,001 to 14,000 ft MSL the maximum holding speed is 230 KIAS [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]] [[29:111|IPH Figure 2-73]]. The inbound leg is 1 minute at or below 14,000 ft MSL; 1½ minutes starts only above 14,000 [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(a)]].

questions.q: After you leave a hold, approach says: 'Descend and maintain 3,000, then reduce speed to 100 knots.' How do you fly it?
options: Slow to 100 knots first, then start down to 3,000
Slow down and descend at the same time, since both are required
Start down to 3,000 and fly any speed until ATC confirms the order
Descend to 3,000 first, then slow to 100 knots and hold it within 10 knots
questions.why: When ATC links a speed change and a descent with the word 'then,' the order given is the order to do them [[33:283|AIM 4-4-12e]]. Once at the assigned speed, keep it within plus or minus 10 knots [[33:283|AIM 4-4-12c]]. If you are unsure how to fly it, ask ATC [[33:283|AIM 4-4-12e]].

questions.q: Your autopilot flies GPS holds, but its bank limit is fixed at 20° and you can't change it. You are told to hold. What should you do?
options: Tell ATC you need extra area for holding
Nothing. The GPS keeps you inside the protected airspace.
Fly 30-second legs so the wider turns still fit
Hold faster so the turns stay at standard rate
questions.why: Bank limits under 25° should not be used unless they can't be changed, the aircraft limits require it, or speed margins need it. If you must hold with less than 25°, advise ATC that additional area for holding is required [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)(4)]]. Shallow bank makes the pattern wider and longer [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(3)]], and the GPS can't warn you when you leave protected airspace [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(b)]].

questions.q: In IMC you are cleared to BOXER intersection, which is not an approach fix: 'Hold east of BOXER as published, expect further clearance via Victor 12 at 1530.' Victor 12 is not your filed route. Your radios fail. What route and timing do you use?
options: Your filed route, leaving BOXER at 1530
Victor 12, leaving BOXER as soon as you arrive
Victor 12, the route ATC told you to expect, leaving BOXER at 1530
Hold at BOXER until ATC answers you, since your clearance ends there
questions.why: With no assigned route beyond the limit, fly the route ATC advised you may expect, before the filed route [[60:482|14 CFR 91.185(c)(1)(iii)]]. When the clearance limit is not where an approach begins, leave it at the EFC time, go to a fix where an approach begins, and start the approach as close as possible to your ETA [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)(ii)]].

questions.q: Holding on an inbound course of 045°, you need a heading of 038° to track it. What heading do you fly on the next outbound leg?
questions.why: Inbound you correct 7° left, so the wind is from the left. Outbound, triple the correction and apply it the other way: 7 x 3 = 21° right. Outbound course 225° + 21° = 246° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]. Correct on the legs, not in the turns [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

questions.q: Departure says: 'Expedite climb to 7,000.' Passing 5,000, you hear: 'Climb and maintain 9,000.' Nothing else is said. How do you climb now?
options: Keep your best rate to 9,000, because the expedite still applies
Level at 7,000 first, then ask if you should expedite to 9,000
Climb at your best rate to 7,000, then at a normal rate to 9,000
Climb at a normal rate; restating the altitude without 'expedite' canceled it
questions.why: If the altitude is changed or restated without an expedite instruction, the expedite is canceled [[33:282|AIM 4-4-10i]]. Then climb promptly at an optimum rate to 1,000 ft below the altitude, then 500 to 1,500 fpm until you reach it [[33:280|AIM 4-4-10d]].

questions.q: You are holding at REDDY, the fix used in lieu of the outer marker on an ILS. The tower is open. Approach says: 'Cleared ILS runway 27 approach, depart REDDY inbound at 1532.' What do you do?
options: Adjust your path in the hold to leave REDDY inbound at 1532, and fly straight in with no procedure turn
Leave REDDY outbound at 1532 and fly the charted procedure turn
Leave the hold right away, since the approach clearance cancels the time
Fly one more full lap, then the procedure turn, so you are stable by 1532
questions.why: A time to depart the fix means timed approaches are in use. Adjust your path within the hold to leave at the exact time [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8k]]. On a timed approach from a holding fix, you may not fly a procedure turn unless you advise ATC and get a clearance for it [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9b1]] [[33:428|AIM 5-4-10a]].

questions.q: Holding in IMC at 6,000 ft, your radios fail. Ten minutes later you break out between layers into clear VFR conditions, with good VFR below. What does 91.185 tell you to do?
options: Stay in the hold until the EFC, then fly the approach
Continue VFR and land as soon as practicable, which need not be an unsuitable airport
Climb back into the clouds and keep holding, since you are still on an IFR clearance
Land at the nearest airport of any kind right away
questions.why: If you meet VFR conditions after the failure, continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable [[60:482|14 CFR 91.185(b)]]. That does not mean as soon as possible: you need not land at an unsuitable airport or just short of your destination [[34:53|AIM 6-4-1]]. After canceling IFR in VFR conditions you may also leave a holding fix [[23:304|IFH 10-13]].

questions.q: You first cross the holding fix at 1512, fly a teardrop entry, and are established on the inbound course at 1515. What do you report to ATC?
options: 1515 and your altitude, when you are established inbound
1513 and your altitude, when you start the outbound timing
Nothing, because you are in radar contact
1512 and your altitude, your first time over the fix
questions.why: The holding entry time reported to ATC is your first time of arrival over the fix [[23:303|IFH 10-12]]. The time and altitude on reaching a holding fix is a report made at all times without an ATC request, radar or not [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3a1(f)]]. Report again when you leave the fix [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]].

questions.q: You are holding at an RNAV waypoint, waiting for an RNAV (GPS) approach. Your GPS fails and you have no other RNAV. What do you tell ATC?
options: Nothing until you leave the hold, because ATC can see you on radar
Squawk 7600 and fly the hold by dead reckoning without calling
Your call sign, the GPS failure, how it limits your IFR flight, and the help you want, such as 'unable RNAV, request amended clearance'
Declare an emergency, because losing GPS in a hold is always an emergency
questions.why: Report any nav malfunction in flight with the aircraft identification, the equipment affected, how much it impairs your IFR capability and the help you want [[60:483|14 CFR 91.187]] [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3a1(h)]]. If you can't meet an RNAV procedure, say so: 'failure of GPS system, unable RNAV, request amended clearance' [[34:10|AIM 5-5-16]]. 7600 is only for two-way radio failure [[34:54|AIM 6-4-2]].

questions.q: In a hold in lieu of a procedure turn, you are cleared for the approach on the outbound leg. You are 1,200 ft above the holding altitude and want one more lap to lose it. What should you do?
options: Fly the extra lap; ATC expects as many laps as you need
Tell ATC you will make another circuit when you get the approach clearance
Descend to the FAF altitude on the outbound leg so no extra lap is needed
Make the extra lap without a call, staying at or above the holding altitude
questions.why: If you are cleared for the approach before you get back to the fix and are at the right altitude, more laps are not needed or expected. If you choose extra laps to lose altitude, it is your job to tell ATC when you get the approach clearance [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9a5]]. You may not descend below the minimum holding altitude until established on the inbound course [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9b3]].

questions.q: You filed IFR with a proposed departure time of 1300. Weather holds you on the ground, and you now plan to leave at 1530. What should you do about your flight plan?
options: Send your new departure time to a flight plan service provider or FSS, since most centers delete plans not activated 2 hours after the proposed time
Nothing. Once filed, an IFR flight plan stays in the system all day.
Nothing. Just ask clearance delivery for your clearance 'as filed' when you are ready.
Cancel it and refile only if ATC calls you to ask about it
questions.why: Most centers delete a proposed flight plan that is not activated within a minimum of 2 hours after the proposed departure time. If you will be 2 hours or more late, give ATC your new time. Since ATC often can't take these revisions by radio, send them to a flight plan service provider or FSS [[33:339|AIM 5-1-13]].

questions.q: Holding in a nonradar area, you pick up ice and need a speed above the maximum holding speed to stay safe. What should you do?
options: Hold at the higher speed; ATC protects extra airspace for icing
Fly 2-minute legs to make up for the extra speed
Tell ATC right away that you can't accept the assigned hold, and ask for another clearance
Hold at the higher speed but shorten each leg to 30 seconds
questions.why: Turbulence or icing may need speeds above the limit, but that can take you outside the protected airspace. Advise ATC immediately and request an alternate clearance; in a nonradar area, tell ATC you cannot accept the assigned hold [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(2)]]. Your own leg changes don't fix it [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]].

questions.q: Center says: 'Descend via the PIKES Two arrival, except after LOBBY, maintain 6,000.' What does this allow?
options: Descend promptly to 6,000 now and hold it along the whole arrival
Fly the arrival's lateral path only, with no descent until ATC gives an altitude
Descend via the whole arrival to its lowest published altitude, then call ATC
Descend at your discretion, meeting the published restrictions to LOBBY, then level at 6,000 until cleared lower
questions.why: 'Descend via' lets you descend at pilot's discretion while meeting all published altitude and speed restrictions. With 'except after (fix), maintain (altitude),' you meet the restrictions until that fix, then maintain the given altitude until cleared to keep descending [[33:394|AIM 5-4-1 Example 4]] [[33:393|AIM 5-4-1]].
